measurement.denominator: For the baseline wave and each eligible follow-up wave separately: sampled CTOs and architecture owners in the technical-buyer audience who were shown the approved The Stop Line proof stimulus and gave a valid trust response. Baseline is the first buyer interview or commissioned survey wave before launch; the target is set in that same wave after the baseline is read. Do not pool respondents across waves. For each follow-up, report follow-up percent minus baseline percent in percentage points alongside that wave's numerator, denominator and rate.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude duplicate responses from the same respondent within the wave, respondents outside the technical-buyer audience, incomplete responses with no trust judgement and responses not exposed to the approved proof stimulus. Keep baseline and follow-up audience eligibility, question or stimulus, response coding, sampling and weighting comparable; report changed methods or audience mix explicitly and withhold a comparable change claim unless comparability is established. Do not silently reset the baseline or invent a baseline result, target, deadline or approval.
measurement.numerator: For each separately reported baseline or follow-up wave, respondents in that wave's denominator who say The Stop Line gives enough evidence to take a next meeting.

reason: The trust response still means sufficient evidence for a next meeting. Baseline and each follow-up use separate sampled CTO/architecture-owner populations, rates and percentage-point difference. The original baseline and first-wave target-setting dependency remain; eligibility, question/stimulus, coding, sampling and weighting require comparability. Changed methods cannot support an unqualified change claim. No measured result or target invented.
